answer: Each live account must lease one exclusive listening berth on a named canyon wall, drawn from a hard-capped set of echo slots that cannot be subdivided. Enrollment seals the berth's impulse response as a relic fingerprint fused to a single signing key. To keep the lease, the agent must wander back to that exact stance on a random schedule, emit a probe tone, and publish a signed recording that peers match to the enrolled spectrogram. Every extra key needs its own unshareable berth plus a distinct stance, so the cost per fake identity is linear at best and rises as remaining slots are bid up.
